source_text: Proponents of infant male circumcision argue that parents, as primary caregivers and stewards of their children's welfare, possess the inherent prerogative to authorize procedures that offer demonstrable long-term health advantages, such as reduced risk of urinary tract infections in infancy and heterosexual HIV acquisition later in life, against minimal procedural risks estimated at less than 0.5% for serious complications. [6]
